scenario.name: CISA AA23-353A, Mandiant & Microsoft — ALPHV / BlackCat (Sphynx) Rust Ransomware, ExMatter Exfiltration & ESXi/Windows Encryption
scenario.overview: Imagine a disciplined heist syndicate carrying three precision tools across a corporate campus. First, a silent courier sweeps high-value folders out to an external van and burns its own footprints behind it; next, the syndicate unlocks a locked briefcase using a unique job passcode, opens cross-room shortcut paths, and shreds every backup binder; finally, the briefcase automatically copies itself down every corridor and basement server rack to snap fast modern locks across both office desks and virtual servers at once. In this scenario (T1048.002, CISA AA23-353A, Mandiant & Microsoft, ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Ransomware, ExMatter Exfiltration & ESXi/Windows Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: exMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then Access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

briefing.storyAnalogy: Imagine a disciplined heist syndicate carrying three precision tools across a corporate campus. First, a silent courier sweeps high-value folders out to an external van and burns its own footprints behind it; next, the syndicate unlocks a locked briefcase using a unique job passcode, opens cross-room shortcut paths, and shreds every backup binder; finally, the briefcase automatically copies itself down every corridor and basement server rack to snap fast modern locks across both office desks and virtual servers at once.

briefing.plainSummary: In this scenario (T1048.002, CISA AA23-353A, Mandiant & Microsoft, ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Ransomware, ExMatter Exfiltration & ESXi/Windows Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: exMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then Access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.
briefing.diagramTopologySummary: The forensic topology spans Node ① (ALPHV / BlackCat Affiliate C2 & ExMatter Drop), Node ② (ExMatter .NET WebDAV/SFTP Exfiltrator), Node ③ (Windows Host , fsutil Symlink + bcat.exe -k), Node ④ (Runtime Process & Artifact Context), Node ⑤ (SMB Shares & ESXi VMFS Datastores , AES/ChaCha20), and Node ⑥ (CISA AA23-353A / Defender XDR & ESXi Sensor) across 3 chronological steps (#1 to #3).

steps.plainTitle: ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration & Self-Erasure Before Encryption
steps.storyAnalogy: Before locking a single door, the affiliate deploys a quiet file-gathering courier disguised as routine office paperwork that filters out junk, packs high-value contracts onto an external truck, and erases its own executable file when finished.
steps.simpleExplanation: Before deploying the encryptor, the ALPHV affiliate stages ExMatter (a compiled .NET exfiltration utility disguised as Svchost.exe orighosting in C:\ProgramData) that enumerates all local and mounted network drives for Office/PDF/CAD documents, uploads them to an attacker-controlled SFTP/WebDAV server over port 443, and spawns powershell.exe to overwrite and delete its own binary on disk (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with ExfiltrationTool=ExMatter .NET SFTP/WebDAV Stealer, TargetedExtensions=.docx.xlsx.pdf.sql.bak.vmdk, AntiForensics=WriteAllBytes Zero-Overwrite + Remove-Item, AdvisoryId=CISA AA23-353A so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes C:\ProgramData\ExMatter.exe (Enumerates .docx.xlsx.pdf.dwg across C:\..Z:\ -> SFTP/WebDAV upload) (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , C:\ProgramData\ExMatter.exe , Enumerates .docx.xlsx.pdf.dwg across C:\..Z:\ -> SFTP/We so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1048.002 during "ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration & Self-Erasure Before Encryption" , Before deploying the encryptor, the ALPHV affiliate stages ExMatter , a compiled while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "[System.IO.File]::WriteAllBytes('C:\ProgramData\ExMatter.exe', New-Object Byte[] 4096); Remove-Item 'C:\ProgramData\ExMatter.exe' -Force" runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1048.002 during "ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration & Self-Erasure Before Encryption" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 across the topology from ALPHV / BlackCat Affiliate C2 & ExMatter Drop and ExMatter .NET WebDAV/SFTP Exfiltrator toward Windows Host , fsutil Symlink + bcat.exe -k and CISA AA23-353A / Defender XDR & ESXi Sensor.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 1 (recording ExfiltrationTool=ExMatter .NET SFTP/WebDAV Stealer, TargetedExtensions=.docx.xlsx.pdf.sql.bak.vmdk, AntiForensics=WriteAllBytes Zero-Overwrite + Remove-Item, AdvisoryId=CISA AA23-353A under T1048.002): Alert on unsigned .NET binaries initiating high-volume outbound SFTP/SSH (port 22) or WebDAV (port 443) transfers followed by PowerShell WriteAllBytes self-wiping commands.

steps.plainTitle: Access-Token Unpacking (-k), fsutil R2R Symlink Enablement & Shadow Wipe
steps.storyAnalogy: The operator unlocks the Rust padlocking briefcase by typing a secret job token on the command line (keeping the inner blueprint scrambled from curious analysts), flips a building shortcut switch so linked remote hallways stay reachable, and shreds every backup snapshot.
steps.simpleExplanation: The operator executes the Rust-compiled BlackCat/Sphynx binary with -k <access_token> (which derives the ChaCha20 key to decrypt the embedded JSON configuration), runs fsutil behavior set SymlinkEvaluation R2L:1 R2R:1 so the encryptor can traverse remote SMB symlinks, increases NetShareSessionPerServer in the registry, and wipes Volume Shadow Copies (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with ParentBinary=bcat_sphynx.exe , Rust ALPHV/BlackCat Sphynx, AccessTokenSwitch=-k 8f94a2c1e0b74d19a3c8f5e2d1b09876, SymlinkEvaluation=R2L:1 R2R:1 Enabled so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).

steps.plainTitle: Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption
steps.storyAnalogy: Armed with stolen master passes packed inside its own pocket, the briefcase marches itself down every office hallway and into the basement hypervisor room, halting running virtual servers and locking both Windows offices and Linux server pods simultaneously.
steps.simpleExplanation: Using credentials harvested via built-in NetExec/Impacket routines (--propagate), BlackCat spreads across SMB shares, clears all Windows Event Logs via wevtutil.exe cl, kills VMware ESXi virtual machines via esxcli vm process kill --type=force, and encrypts files using hardware-accelerated AES-128-CTR or ChaCha20 with RSA-2048 key wrapping (RECOVER-<ext>-FILES.txt) (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with RansomwareFamily=ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Variant, EncryptionMode=AES-128-CTR , Hardware AES-NI / ChaCha20 + RSA-2048, RansomNote=RECOVER-sphynx-FILES.txt so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes for /F "tokens=*" %1 in ('wevtutil.exe el') do wevtutil.exe cl "%1" (which invokes the Windows Event Collector CLI utility , wevtutil.exe with the cl , clear-log or el , enum-logs parameter to instruct svchost.exe , EventL so that attempts anti-forensic indicator removal , T1486 during "Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption" by wiping recorded Windows Security, System, PowerShell, or Sysmon audit trails, which immediately causes the OS to write Security EventID 1102 or System EventID 104 and USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION in $UsnJrnl:$J). Next, the follow-up artifact esxcli vm process list && esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=419820 runs (which executes VMware ESXi hypervisor management commands , esxcli vm process list && esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=419820 via the root so that releases exclusive hypervisor locks on Guest VM flat disk files , *-flat.vmdk, *.nvram · T1486 during "Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption" so the ransomware encryptor can overwrite virtual disks at high speed, leaving audit trails in /var/log/shell.log and /var/log/hostd.log).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 11 (recording RansomwareFamily=ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Variant, EncryptionMode=AES-128-CTR , Hardware AES-NI / ChaCha20 + RSA-2048, RansomNote=RECOVER-sphynx-FILES.txt under T1486): Segment ESXi management interfaces onto isolated jump VLANs with MFA, enforce SMB signing, and forward Windows Event Logs in real time prior to wevtutil.exe cl truncation.
